new_statements.translation: Studies of word stress and of sentence-level intonation are still lacking for Buli and could well be relevant for the (diachronic) assessment of the tone system. Accent is characterised by intensity and is not tied to quantity. It mostly occupies a penultimate position in the word, which largely conforms to the situation Olawsky describes for Dagbani (cf. 1999: 172ff.).

new_statements.rule_in_words: Buli is a three-tone language (L, M, H) with lexical and grammatical tone; alongside tone, the author notes an intensity-based (not quantity-sensitive) word accent that mostly falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, while explicitly stating that no systematic study of Buli word stress exists yet. Provisional placement reading: penultimate (fixed: penultimate syllable), low confidence.
new_statements.exceptions: 'meist' (mostly) penultimate — no exceptions specified; the author flags the observation as preliminary and untested.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('im Wort'); made in the research-state section of a tonology-oriented dissertation on the Wiaga (Wieni) variety; no examples, no instrumental data.
new_statements.identity_note: Schwarz 2005 describes the Buli of Wiaga (Wieni dialect) specifically; Buli (Ghana) has no separate Glottolog dialect code for Wieni under buli1254. Akanlig-Pare's 1988 MA treats the Wiani dialect (same variety, different spelling). Prost's 'Le bulba' (1970) is listed by Glottolog under buli1254 but was not verified here.

tone_statements.citation: Angsongna, Alexander, Samuel Alhassan Issah, Hasiyatu Abubakari, Darius Adjong, Abraham Kwesi Bisilki, Samuel Awinkene Atintono & Adams Bodomo. 2026. Tone in Mabia Languages: Structure and Processes. Languages 11(5): 104. doi:10.3390/languages11050104
tone_statements.quote: Dagaare and Dagbani exhibit a two-tone system (high and low), with an additional down-stepped high tone. Kusaal, Likpakpaln, and Buli employ a three-tone system (high, mid, and low), while the tonal status of Gurenɛ remains contested... The mid tone, though relatively less productive, appears to represent a later innovation within the group. The mid tone performs both lexical and grammatical functions.
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones H, M, L (Buli grouped with Kusaal, Likpakpaln); M partly grammatical.

tone_statements.citation: Akanlig-Pare, George & Michael Kenstowicz. 2003. Tone in Buli. In Akanlig-Pare & Kenstowicz (eds.), Studies in Buli Grammar (MIT Working Papers on Endangered and Less Familiar Languages 4), 1-34. Preprint (68 pp.) from Kenstowicz's MIT page.
tone_statements.quote: Buli distinguishes three lexical tones: high, mid, and low. There is no downstep. The language has a surface rising tone but it is a predictable variant of an underlying high tone. While nouns and adjectives contrast for the three tonal levels, verbs have no lexical contrasts in tone. However, tense and aspectual distinctions are encoded tonally making for an intricate set of tonal paradigms for verbs. The syllable is the tone-bearing unit in Buli. Even though the language combines a vowel length distinction with an optional coda of one or two consonants, there is no underlying tonal contrast as a function of syllable shape.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2 'Tonal Contrasts', preprint p. 2; = SAL 31(1/2) p. 56
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones H M L; surface rise = L spread onto H; no downstep; verbs lexically toneless, tense/aspect by tonal morphemes (H+L Agr, L Tns); unlinked tones deleted ('banning floating tones'). F0 s.9.
